  5. 513.2 · Spheres · completing the square
    The equation x2+y2+z2−6x+4y−12=0x^2+y^2+z^2-6x+4y-12=0x2+y2+z2−6x+4y−12=0 describes a sphere. Find its centre and radius.

(x−3)2+(y+2)2+z2=25(x-3)^2+(y+2)^2+z^2=25(x−3)2+(y+2)2+z2=25. Centre (3,−2,0)(3,-2,0)(3,−2,0), radius 555.

    TrapSign flip on the centre. (x−3)² means the centre coordinate is +3, not −3.

    L1:  x=1+t,  y=2−t,  z=3+2tL_1:\;x=1+t,\;y=2-t,\;z=3+2tL1​:x=1+t,y=2−t,z=3+2t and L2:  x=2+2s,  y=1−2s,  z=6+4sL_2:\;x=2+2s,\;y=1-2s,\;z=6+4sL2​:x=2+2s,y=1−2s,z=6+4s. These two lines are

    Now decide parallel-and-distinct versus identical: is L2L_2L2​'s point (2,1,6)(2,1,6)(2,1,6) on L1L_1L1​? From xxx: 1+t=2⇒t=11+t=2\Rightarrow t=11+t=2⇒t=1, giving (2,1,5)(2,1,5)(2,1,5) on L1L_1L1​ — not (2,1,6)(2,1,6)(2,1,6).

  2. 213.6 · Quadric surfaces · identify
    Identify the surface x24+y29−z2=1\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}-z^2=14x2​+9y2​−z2=1.

    Answer C

    Count the minus signs among the squared terms: exactly one, and the right side is 111. One minus ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ hyperboloid of one sheet — the connected cooling-tower shape. Check with a trace: setting z=0z=0z=0 gives the ellipse x24+y29=1\tfrac{x^2}{4}+\tfrac{y^2}{9}=14x2​+9y2​=1, a real curve, so the surface exists at the waist and is not in two pieces.

    TrapTwo minus signs would be two sheets; right side 0 would be a cone.

  3. 313.6 · Quadric surfaces · traces
    What is the trace of the cone z2=x2+y2z^2=x^2+y^2z2=x2+y2 in the plane z=3z=3z=3?

    Answer A

    Substitute z=3z=3z=3: 9=x2+y29=x^2+y^29=x2+y2, a circle of radius 333. The vertical traces are different: setting y=0y=0y=0 gives z2=x2z^2=x^2z2=x2, i.e. the pair of lines z=±xz=\pm xz=±x — which is why the surface is a cone and not a paraboloid.

(∇×F)⋅n=33=3(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot\mathbf n=\tfrac{3}{\sqrt3}=\sqrt3(∇×F)⋅n=3​3​=3​, a constant. The triangle's area is 32\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}23​​, so ∮=3⋅32=32\oint=\sqrt3\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=\dfrac{3}{2}∮=3​⋅23​​=23​.

    TrapUsing the un-normalised ⟨1,1,1⟩ as n, or the projected area instead of the true area.

    Review §17.7 in the study guide

  2. 217.7 · Stokes' theorem
    SSS is any upward-oriented smooth surface whose boundary is the circle x2+y2=4x^2+y^2=4x2+y2=4 in the plane z=1z=1z=1, oriented counterclockwise seen from above. For F=⟨−y,  x,  z2⟩\mathbf F=\langle -y,\;x,\;z^2\rangleF=⟨−y,x,z2⟩, find ∬S(∇×F)⋅n dS\displaystyle\iint_S(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot\mathbf n\,dS∬S​(∇×F)⋅ndS.

    Answer C

    Stokes turns the surface integral into one lap around the rim, so the surface itself is irrelevant. Parametrize C:  r(t)=⟨2cos⁡t, 2sin⁡t, 1⟩C:\;\mathbf r(t)=\langle 2\cos t,\,2\sin t,\,1\rangleC:r(t)=⟨2cost,2sint,1⟩, r  ⁣′=⟨−2sin⁡t, 2cos⁡t, 0⟩\mathbf r\,\!\prime=\langle-2\sin t,\,2\cos t,\,0\rangler′=⟨−2sint,2cost,0⟩. F(r(t))=⟨−2sin⁡t, 2cos⁡t, 1⟩\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))=\langle-2\sin t,\,2\cos t,\,1\rangleF(r(t))=⟨−2sint,2cost,1⟩. F⋅r  ⁣′=4sin⁡2t+4cos⁡2t=4\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf r\,\!\prime=4\sin^2t+4\cos^2t=4F⋅r′=4sin2t+4cos2t=4, so ∮=4(2π)=8π\oint=4(2\pi)=8\pi∮=4(2π)=8π. (Equivalently ∇×F=⟨0,0,2⟩\nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle0,0,2\rangle∇×F=⟨0,0,2⟩ and the flux through the disk is 2⋅π(2)2=8π2\cdot\pi(2)^2=8\pi2⋅π(2)2=8π.)

    TrapTrying to build the unknown surface. Stokes says only the rim matters.

    Review §17.7 in the study guide

  3. 317.7 · Stokes' theorem
    CCC is the boundary of the first-octant part of the plane x+y+z=1x+y+z=1x+y+z=1, oriented counterclockwise viewed from above. For F=⟨y,  z,  x⟩\mathbf F=\langle y,\;z,\;x\rangleF=⟨y,z,x⟩, find ∮CF⋅dr\displaystyle\oint_C\mathbf F\cdot d\mathbf r∮C​F⋅dr.

    Answer B

    ∇×F=⟨−1,−1,−1⟩\nabla\times\mathbf F=\langle-1,-1,-1\rangle∇×F=⟨−1,−1,−1⟩. The triangle lies in x+y+z=1x+y+z=1x+y+z=1 with upward unit normal n=13⟨1,1,1⟩\mathbf n=\tfrac1{\sqrt3}\langle1,1,1\ranglen=3​1​⟨1,1,1⟩. (∇×F)⋅n=−33=−3(\nabla\times\mathbf F)\cdot\mathbf n=-\tfrac{3}{\sqrt3}=-\sqrt3(∇×F)⋅n=−3​3​=−3​, constant. Triangle area =32=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=23​​, so ∮=−3⋅32=−32\oint=-\sqrt3\cdot\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=-\dfrac32∮=−3​⋅23​​=−23​.

    TrapLosing the sign. A negative circulation is a real answer, not an error.

  4. 417.8 · Divergence theorem
    Find the net outward flux of F=⟨x2,  2y,  3z⟩\mathbf F=\langle x^2,\;2y,\;3z\rangleF=⟨x2,2y,3z⟩ through the surface of the box [0,2]×[0,1]×[0,1][0,2]\times[0,1]\times[0,1][0,2]×[0,1]×[0,1].

    Answer C

    div⁡F=2x+2+3=2x+5\operatorname{div}\mathbf F=2x+2+3=2x+5divF=2x+2+3=2x+5. ∭E(2x+5) dV=∫01 ⁣ ⁣∫01 ⁣ ⁣∫02(2x+5) dx dy dz=[x2+5x]02=4+10=14\displaystyle\iiint_E(2x+5)\,dV=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^2(2x+5)\,dx\,dy\,dz =\big[x^2+5x\big]_0^2=4+10=14∭E​(2x+5)dV=∫01​∫01​∫02​(2x+5)dxdydz=[x2+5x]02​=4+10=14.

    TrapIntegrating six faces by hand. One triple integral replaces all of them.

    Review §17.8 in the study guide

  5. 517.8 · Divergence theorem · spherical
    Find the outward flux of F=⟨x,  y,  z⟩\mathbf F=\langle x,\;y,\;z\rangleF=⟨x,y,z⟩ across the sphere of radius 222 centred at the origin.

    Answer D

    div⁡F=1+1+1=3\operatorname{div}\mathbf F=1+1+1=3divF=1+1+1=3, a constant, so the triple integral is 3×(volume)=3⋅43π(2)3=32π3\times(\text{volume})=3\cdot\tfrac43\pi(2)^3=32\pi3×(volume)=3⋅34​π(2)3=32π. Check directly: on the sphere F⋅n=∣r∣=2\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n=|\mathbf r|=2F⋅n=∣r∣=2, and the area is 4π(2)2=16π4\pi(2)^2=16\pi4π(2)2=16π, giving 2⋅16π=32π2\cdot16\pi=32\pi2⋅16π=32π ✓.

  6. 617.8 · Divergence theorem · cylinder
    Find the outward flux of F=⟨x, y, z⟩\mathbf F=\langle x,\,y,\,z\rangleF=⟨x,y,z⟩ through the closed surface of the solid cylinder x2+y2≤1x^2+y^2\le1x2+y2≤1, 0≤z≤20\le z\le20≤z≤2.

    Answer D

    div⁡F=3\operatorname{div}\mathbf F=3divF=3, constant, so the flux is 3×volume3\times\text{volume}3×volume. Volume =π(1)2(2)=2π=\pi(1)^2(2)=2\pi=π(1)2(2)=2π, giving 6π6\pi6π. Doing it by faces would mean three separate surface integrals — the theorem replaces all of them.

    TrapForgetting the two flat caps if you insist on computing faces directly.

    Review §17.8 in the study guide

  7. 717.8 · Divergence theorem · capping
    SSS is the paraboloid z=4−x2−y2z=4-x^2-y^2z=4−x2−y2 with z≥0z\ge0z≥0, oriented upward — it is open at the bottom. Find the flux of F=⟨x, y, z⟩\mathbf F=\langle x,\,y,\,z\rangleF=⟨x,y,z⟩ through SSS.

    Answer D

    Cap it with the disk D:  z=0,  x2+y2≤4D:\;z=0,\;x^2+y^2\le4D:z=0,x2+y2≤4, oriented downward so the union is a sealed outward-oriented bag. Volume: ∫02π ⁣ ⁣∫02(4−r2)r dr dθ=2π[2r2−r44]02=8π\displaystyle\int_0^{2\pi}\!\!\int_0^2(4-r^2)r\,dr\,d\theta=2\pi\big[2r^2-\tfrac{r^4}{4}\big]_0^2=8\pi∫02π​∫02​(4−r2)rdrdθ=2π[2r2−4r4​]02​=8π. div⁡F=3\operatorname{div}\mathbf F=3divF=3, so the sealed flux is 3(8π)=24π3(8\pi)=24\pi3(8π)=24π. On the cap z=0z=0z=0: n=⟨0,0,−1⟩\mathbf n=\langle0,0,-1\ranglen=⟨0,0,−1⟩ and F⋅n=−z=0\mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n=-z=0F⋅n=−z=0, so the cap contributes nothing. Therefore the flux through SSS alone is 24π−0=24π24\pi-0=24\pi24π−0=24π.

    TrapApplying the divergence theorem to S by itself. It is not closed — you must cap it, then subtract the cap.
